description: A guided, verified build for a custom Wideband operator machine.

stages.title: Prepare
stages.description: Remove the avoidable account and machine blockers before installation begins.

steps.title: Send the preparation sheet
steps.description: Send PREP.md to the client at least one day before the build.

steps.title: Create a separate agent Apple Account
steps.description: Create a separate agent Apple Account when you are ready to activate iMessage. Local core and Fleetdeck can be prepared first.
steps.note: The agent Apple Account must differ from the Apple Account used on your personal iPhone.

client_guide.intro: A separate Apple Account is required for agent texting. You can do this later while Wideband prepares the local tools, first job, and Fleetdeck.
client_guide.purpose: A separate sender makes the first text and every reply unambiguous on your phone.
client_guide.success: You can sign into the agent Apple Account yourself and receive its verification codes. The account is different from your personal phone's account.
instructions: Create or choose an Apple Account for the agent Mac that is separate from the Apple Account on your personal iPhone.
Use an email address you control and complete Apple's account verification on Apple's page.
Keep the password and verification codes in your own password manager. Never enter them in Wideband Setup.
Return here when the separate agent account is ready. Messages sign-in and a real two-way text test are separate later checks.
client_guide.privacy: Wideband saves only your confirmation. Passwords and verification codes stay with Apple.
client_guide.acknowledgment_label: I confirm this agent Apple Account is different from the Apple Account on my personal iPhone.

steps.title: Collect the build identity
steps.description: Have the company short name, GitHub username, commit email, phone for briefs, work repository, and graph pack ready.

steps.title: Confirm management and migration status
steps.description: Confirm the Mac is not MDM-managed, the client is an administrator, and whether data will be migrated from another Mac.
steps.note: Any one of these answers can change the build path.

steps.title: Complete macOS Setup Assistant
steps.description: Connect power and Wi-Fi, create the administrator account, and finish macOS updates. Agent Apple Account sign-in can follow local setup.

client_guide.intro: Confirm this Mac is ready to become your always-on Wideband operator machine.
client_guide.purpose: The local tools need a stable administrator session. The dedicated agent Apple Account is required later for Messages.
client_guide.success: The Mac is powered, online, updated, and the current macOS user is an administrator. Agent Apple Account sign-in may still be pending.
instructions: Keep the Mac connected to power and a reliable network.
If the dedicated agent Apple Account is ready, sign into it. Do not use your personal iPhone account for the agent. If it is not ready, finish macOS setup and return to agent account sign-in later.
After a delayed or partially completed Apple Account sign-in, open Messages separately and confirm its iMessage account. Apple Account and Messages sign-in are two distinct checks.
Confirm your current macOS user is an administrator.
Finish any pending Migration Assistant or macOS update before continuing.

steps.title: Resolve Migration Assistant
steps.description: Skip migration unless it was planned. If migration is required, finish it completely before continuing.
steps.note: Migrated dotfiles and PATH entries can quietly conflict with this build.

stages.title: Identify
stages.description: Give the machine one coherent identity, then capture the operator judgment that cannot be templated.

steps.title: Name your OS and head agent
steps.description: Choose an OS display name, an editable head-agent name, an AI provider, and the first job to prepare for.

client_guide.intro: Name your Wideband OS and head agent, choose an AI provider, and give the agent its first job.
client_guide.purpose: These choices make the setup personal and tell Wideband which provider and first-job tools to prepare.
client_guide.success: Your four choices are saved privately on this Mac. The OS name is a display name, not a change to the Mac hostname.
instructions: Enter a short display name for your OS, such as Aurora.
Name your head agent, such as Trace. You can edit its name later.
Select Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, or Grok Build. Preview providers wait for runtime verification.
Choose Research, Build a website, or Proposal (advanced), then save.

steps.title: Run the bootstrap
steps.description: Install the agent, start Homebrew, fetch this setup repository, and write the build identity.
steps.note: The packaged guide opens immediately and shows live bootstrap progress before Homebrew or Apple Command Line Tools are ready.

steps.title: Review the identity file
steps.description: Confirm every value is correct before it is rendered into services and agent configuration.

steps.title: Connect your AI provider
steps.description: Sign into the provider you selected before the head agent starts.
steps.note: The provider choice is saved locally; a live head-agent reply still requires runtime and account proof.

client_guide.intro: Connect the AI provider you selected. Wideband checks the local tool and runtime before it can answer a text.
client_guide.purpose: The head agent must be signed in before it can read your first text and produce a reply.
client_guide.success: The selected provider is authenticated and the head agent answers a real text on your phone.
instructions: Review the selected provider and its setup status below.
Complete sign-in directly with that provider when Wideband offers its verified setup path.
Return here when Wideband can verify the account and head-agent runtime.
client_guide.privacy: Passwords and verification codes stay with your provider.

steps.title: Complete the operator interview
steps.description: Capture responsibilities, collaboration style, approval boundaries, communication preferences, and recurring priorities.

steps.title: Review the generated agent profile
steps.description: Preview and approve USER.md before it becomes part of the agent's standing context.

client_guide.intro: This is the custom part: tell the agent how to work with you, where it may act, and where it must stop and ask.
instructions: Open the profile interview and answer in plain language.
Be specific about approval boundaries, spending, external messages, and production changes.
Do not enter passwords, API keys, or project secrets.
Preview the profile, approve it, then return here to confirm your review.
client_guide.privacy: The profile is stored only on this Mac.

stages.title: Connect
stages.description: Guide the client through the macOS and account actions no installer should impersonate.

steps.title: Enable Remote Login
steps.description: Open General → Sharing and turn on Remote Login.

client_guide.intro: Remote Login gives the Wideband operator a private command-line support path without exposing it to the public internet.
client_guide.purpose: This is the recovery path Wideband can use when the visual interface is unavailable or a background service needs repair.
client_guide.success: Remote Login is on, remote-user Full Disk Access is off, and only the named administrator is allowed.
instructions: Select Open System Settings.
Turn Remote Login on, then select its info button.
Turn off Allow full disk access for remote users unless Wideband has explicitly requested it for an approved workflow.
Under Allow access for, choose Only these users. Remove the Administrators group and add only the intended individual administrator account.
Return here and let Wideband verify the setting.

steps.title: Enable secure Screen Sharing
steps.description: Enable Apple's built-in Screen Sharing for visual support over the private tailnet.

client_guide.intro: Apple Screen Sharing lets your Wideband operator see and control this Mac when visual help is needed.
client_guide.purpose: Visual support makes permission and account troubleshooting possible without asking you to describe every screen over the phone.
client_guide.success: Screen Sharing is on for only the intended administrator, with legacy VNC-password access left off.
instructions: Select Open Screen Sharing settings.
Turn Screen Sharing on. If Remote Management is on, macOS requires you to turn it off first.
Under Allow access for, choose Only these users and keep only the intended administrator account.
Leave the legacy VNC password option off unless Wideband explicitly asks for it.
Return here and let Wideband verify the system service.
client_guide.privacy: The service is restricted to the account you choose and will be reached through the private tailnet.

steps.title: Grant Full Disk Access
steps.description: Grant the installed Wideband Agent access to protected local data needed for approved workflows.

client_guide.intro: Full Disk Access lets the Wideband Agent work with protected files and Messages data you explicitly authorize on this Mac.
client_guide.purpose: Approved workflows need one stable, branded app—not Terminal or a changing script—to reach protected local data.
client_guide.success: Wideband Agent is enabled in Full Disk Access and its harmless local read check passes.
instructions: Select Show Wideband Agent. System Settings and the installed agent will open together.
In Full Disk Access, select + and add the revealed Wideband Agent.app if it is not already listed.
Turn Wideband Agent on and approve the macOS confirmation.
Return here and run the check. Wideband reads one byte from a protected system database only to prove the grant.
client_guide.privacy: This is a local macOS grant. The permission check does not copy or transmit protected data.

steps.title: Grant Accessibility
steps.description: Ask macOS to authorize the installed Wideband Agent for approved visible-control automation.

client_guide.intro: Accessibility permission allows approved local automation to operate visible controls when a task requires it.
client_guide.purpose: This lets the branded Wideband Agent operate visible controls for workflows you approve while keeping the grant away from general developer tools.
client_guide.success: Wideband Agent appears enabled under Accessibility and confirms the grant itself.
instructions: Select Request Accessibility and wait a few seconds. The real macOS alert and Accessibility entry will name Wideband Agent.
Choose Open System Settings when macOS displays the alert.
Turn on Wideband Agent in the Accessibility list. If you dismissed the alert earlier, use Open Accessibility Settings below.
Return here; the same agent will verify its access.

actions.label: 1. Request Accessibility
actions.message: Wideband Agent requested access. Respond to the macOS alert, then enable Wideband Agent in the list.

actions.label: 2. Open Accessibility Settings
actions.message: Accessibility settings opened. Turn on Wideband Agent, then return here.

client_guide.privacy: Only the installed Wideband Agent receives this grant—not Terminal, Python, or every development tool.

steps.title: Grant Screen Recording
steps.description: Ask macOS to authorize the installed Wideband Agent for visual verification.

client_guide.intro: Screen Recording permission is required for browser screenshots and visual verification; it does not start a recording by itself.
client_guide.purpose: Wideband needs to verify what is visibly on screen during approved browser and desktop workflows.
client_guide.success: Wideband Agent is enabled under Screen & System Audio Recording and a fresh capture check passes.
instructions: Select Request Screen Access and wait a few seconds. The real macOS alert will explicitly name Wideband Agent.
Choose Open System Settings, then turn on Wideband Agent in Screen & System Audio Recording.
If you dismissed the alert earlier, use Open Recording Settings below and enable Wideband Agent there.
If macOS asks to quit and reopen the agent, approve it; the next check launches a fresh copy.
Return here so the same agent can verify the grant.

actions.label: 1. Request Screen Access
actions.message: Wideband Agent requested screen access. Respond to the macOS alert, then enable Wideband Agent in the list.

actions.label: 2. Open Recording Settings
actions.message: Screen & System Audio Recording settings opened. Turn on Wideband Agent, then return here.

client_guide.privacy: The grant belongs only to Wideband Agent and does not start continuous recording.

steps.title: Approve Messages automation
steps.description: Ask macOS to approve Wideband Agent controlling Messages.

client_guide.intro: macOS must explicitly allow the local automation layer to ask Messages to perform approved actions.
client_guide.purpose: This is the protected Apple permission that later allows approved briefs and alerts to use Messages.
client_guide.success: The macOS dialog names Wideband Agent, you select Allow, and the account-count verification passes without sending or reading a message.
instructions: Select 1. Open Messages. Finish sign-in and dismiss any first-run panels, including Shared with You or Focus status prompts.
Return here and select 2. Show macOS prompt.
When macOS says Wideband Agent wants to control Messages, select Allow.
No message is sent by this check.
Return here so Wideband Agent can verify the approval.

actions.label: 1. Open Messages
actions.message: Finish Messages sign-in and any first-run panels, then return here.

actions.label: 2. Show macOS prompt
actions.message: Choose Allow in the macOS dialog, then return here to verify it.

client_guide.privacy: This consent check asks Messages only for its configured-account count. It does not read or send any message or conversation content.

steps.title: Allow background items
steps.description: Allow the Wideband LaunchAgents under Login Items & Extensions.

client_guide.intro: After binding your text, Wideband checks that all four background messaging services loaded.
client_guide.purpose: The listener, router, head-agent keeper, and guarded outbox must keep working when this window closes.
client_guide.success: The live check sees all four messaging services loaded. If macOS lists Wideband under Allow in the Background, it is enabled.
instructions: Bind your owner-only iMessage chat first. Wideband loads the messaging jobs only after that binding succeeds.
Open Login Items & Extensions. If macOS lists Wideband under Allow in the Background, leave it enabled.
Select Check background services. If the check fails, review Login Items and use Setup tools to repair the service installation.

steps.title: Sign into Messages
steps.description: Sign into iMessage with the separate agent Apple Account.

client_guide.intro: Sign Messages into the agent account so your phone can text the agent as a separate person.
client_guide.purpose: The agent Mac must receive iMessages at an identity different from your personal phone.
client_guide.success: Messages shows the separate agent Apple Account and an ordinary iMessage reaches this Mac. An agent reply is verified later.
instructions: Open Messages and sign in with the separate agent Apple Account. Complete Apple's verification personally.
In Messages settings, confirm the separate account's reachable addresses are enabled.
From your personal iPhone, send the agent account one ordinary iMessage and confirm it appears on this Mac. The later two-way agent test proves the runtime.
client_guide.privacy: Sign-in stays inside Apple's Messages app. Wideband does not collect your Apple Account email, password, or verification code.

steps.title: Connect your text to the head agent
steps.description: Bind one fresh, owner-only iMessage chat and start the persistent head agent and guarded reply worker.

client_guide.intro: Send one new iMessage from your personal phone. Wideband will bind only that exact one-to-one chat to your agent.
client_guide.purpose: The listener needs one verified chat before it can deliver your text to the head agent or send a reply.
client_guide.success: The live check sees the exact owner chat, a persistent head-agent session, and all four guarded messaging services.
instructions: Confirm this Mac's Messages app is using the separate agent Apple Account and Wideband has staged the private head-agent workspace.
From your personal iPhone, send the agent account a new iMessage now. Use an individual chat, not a group chat, and keep it within ten minutes of binding.
Select Bind my text below. Wideband checks that the sender matches your private owner phone and that there is exactly one eligible chat.
Wait while Wideband loads the listener, router, persistent head agent, and guarded outbox. If a service is blocked, open Login Items & Extensions and allow Wideband in the background.
Select Check connection. A reply on your phone is the next proof.
client_guide.privacy: Binding uses the owner phone already saved in your private build identity. This guide never asks for your Apple password, code, or message contents.

steps.title: Keep scheduled work awake
steps.description: Disable system and disk sleep so scheduled loops can run reliably.

steps.title: Prove email works
steps.description: Send the operator a message and confirm it arrives before attempting downstream verification flows.

client_guide.intro: Email needs to work before the other services can send verification or recovery messages.
instructions: Open Mail and add the dedicated work email if needed.
Send a message to an address you can check from another device.
Reply to it and confirm the reply arrives on this Mac.

steps.title: Sign into browser accounts
steps.description: Sign into GitHub, Anthropic, Tailscale, Vercel, and Supabase with the intended identities.

client_guide.intro: Sign into each provider in the default browser so later setup can use the accounts you own.
instructions: Use the intended GitHub identity everywhere GitHub sign-in is available.
Complete every two-factor prompt and account confirmation.
Leave each successful dashboard tab open until you return here.
client_guide.privacy: Wideband opens the official pages; it never receives the credentials you enter.

steps.title: Install standalone Tailscale
steps.description: For private phone access, install the standalone download, approve its macOS network extension, and sign in. Local Fleetdeck does not require Tailscale.

steps.title: Keep Tailscale connected after restart
steps.description: Enable Tailscale's native Start on Login setting and confirm the private connection returns after a Mac restart.

client_guide.intro: Your private phone link needs Tailscale to reconnect when you sign back into this Mac.
client_guide.purpose: The Mac must rejoin your tailnet after a restart so your phone can reach its private pages.
client_guide.success: After you restart and sign into the Mac, Tailscale shows Connected without manually launching the app or running a command.
instructions: Open the standalone Tailscale app's Settings and turn on Start on Login.
Confirm Tailscale is connected, then restart the Mac and sign into your usual macOS user.
Wait for Tailscale to reconnect on its own. Check its menu bar status before manually launching the app or running tailscale up.
If it stays disconnected, leave this step open and tell Wideband; signing in to Tailscale once does not prove restart persistence.

steps.title: Enable tailnet HTTPS
steps.description: Enable HTTPS certificates in the tailnet admin console and create a test serve mapping.
steps.command: tailscale serve --bg --https=8790 http://127.0.0.1:8790 && tailscale serve status

steps.title: Prove the phone path
steps.description: Open the test URL on the client's phone and confirm there is a real padlock with no warning.
steps.note: A successful curl from the Mac does not prove this path.

client_guide.intro: Wideband will provide a private tailnet URL after the secure phone path is ready.
instructions: Open the URL on your phone while connected to Tailscale.
Confirm the page opens with a real padlock and no certificate warning.
After the Mac restarts and Tailscale reconnects, open the same private HTTPS link on your phone again.
Do not approve or bypass a browser security warning—tell Wideband instead.

stages.title: Install
stages.description: Run the repeatable installation and prove the resulting objects exist and are healthy.

steps.title: Install the core toolchain
steps.description: Let bootstrap finish Homebrew and the Brewfile, then verify every required CLI.

steps.title: Install the first-text foundation
steps.description: Install only Wideband Agent, imsg, tmux, and the guarded iMessage service templates before optional full-stack tools.

steps.title: Authenticate the GitHub CLI
steps.description: Authenticate gh and confirm it is the one identity named in the build profile.

steps.title: Reconcile the Wideband layer
steps.description: Install agent context, tmux configuration, standing loops, and fleetdeck from the repository.

steps.title: Stage the private head-agent runtime
steps.description: Install imsg and stage the owner-bound workspace using the saved names and private build identity.

steps.title: Verify the Claude layer
steps.description: Prove the status line, settings, parser, and standing context were installed correctly.

steps.title: Finish VS Code setup
steps.description: Open VS Code, install its shell command, and grant Full Disk Access.

steps.title: Install the tmux workspace
steps.description: Load TPM plugins and confirm the command center, configuration, and standard exist.
steps.note: Inside tmux, press Ctrl-a and then Shift-i once to fetch the plugin set.

steps.title: Start the standing sessions
steps.description: Apply the curated session standard and confirm every concern is represented.

steps.title: Verify background loops
steps.description: Confirm each LaunchAgent is loaded and its most recent exit was clean.

steps.title: Verify fleetdeck
steps.description: Confirm the board is installed and resolves its machine dynamically from Tailscale.

steps.title: Verify the shell path
steps.description: Open a new Terminal window and prove every installed tool is discoverable.

stages.title: Customize
stages.description: Connect the operator's actual work, secrets, deployment surface, and recoverable knowledge.

steps.title: Prepare the chosen first job
steps.description: Prepare the selected research, website, or proposal starting point locally, and register the website preview in Fleetdeck when selected. Messaging can remain pending.

steps.title: Install the local Fleetdeck phone view
steps.description: Install the local customer Fleetdeck board after the first job is prepared. Tailscale sign-in, HTTPS, and Add to Home Screen remain separate owner proofs.

steps.title: Clone the work repository
steps.description: Clone the configured work repository to ~/app and install its dependencies.
steps.command: source ~/.sop-vars && git clone "$WORK_REPO" ~/app && cd ~/app && npm install

steps.title: Configure project secrets
steps.description: Seed .env.local and enter the Supabase URL, anon key, service-role key, site URL, and any app-specific values directly on this machine.
steps.note: Secrets are never stored in installer state or support logs.

steps.title: Apply migrations deliberately
steps.description: Apply migrations individually and verify the database objects—not only the migration ledger.
steps.note: Do not run a blanket db push against a project with an existing ledger.

steps.title: Run the application tests
steps.description: Run the repository's test suite and resolve failures before deployment.

steps.title: Serve development to the tailnet
steps.description: Start the development server on 0.0.0.0 and map it through Tailscale HTTPS.

steps.title: Link and verify Vercel
steps.description: Authenticate, link the intended project, and confirm the project ID, environment variables, and domain are real.

steps.title: Curate the standing workspace
steps.description: Keep one tmux session per concern, point website at the actual work root, and remove concerns this operator does not need.

steps.title: Build the knowledge graph
steps.description: When included in the engagement, declare the load-bearing roots, build the index, and run the reconstitution drill.

stages.title: Prove
stages.description: A build is finished only when its real user paths and scheduled behavior have been observed.

steps.title: Run the quick verification
steps.description: Check local machine state without waiting on network-bound services.

steps.title: Run the full verification
steps.description: Run every assertion and work remaining failures in phase order.

steps.title: Reboot and prove persistence
steps.description: Restart the Mac, then confirm the standard tmux sessions and background healthcheck returned without manual repair.

steps.title: Open the board from the phone
steps.description: Open fleetdeck from the client's phone, confirm trusted HTTPS, and add it to the home screen.

client_guide.intro: Your private command board should behave like an app from your phone.
instructions: Open the board URL Wideband provides while Tailscale is connected.
Confirm the board loads without a certificate warning.
Use Add to Home Screen, then launch it from the new icon once.

steps.title: Receive a real reply from your agent
steps.description: Send a new text from your phone and confirm the head agent replies in that chat.

client_guide.intro: Text the agent from your phone and wait for its answer in the same iMessage chat.
client_guide.purpose: A phone reply proves the listener, binding, agent session, and guarded outbox worked together.
client_guide.success: You personally saw a reply from the agent account on your phone, and Wideband's live runtime checks pass.
instructions: From your personal iPhone, send the agent account a fresh question such as 'What can you help me with today?'
Wait for the head agent's answer to arrive in that same chat on your phone.
Only confirm this step after you personally see the answer. If it does not arrive, leave this step open and use Setup tools.

steps.title: Generate the build record
steps.description: Capture machine, operator, installer release, verification summary, progress, and every recorded deviation.

steps.title: Observe the first scheduled brief
steps.description: The next morning, confirm the usage brief arrived through the intended channel.
steps.note: Until a scheduled job has fired once, it is installed—not working.

client_guide.intro: The first scheduled brief is the final proof that the always-on system survived the night.
instructions: Leave the Mac plugged in, awake, and online overnight.
Confirm the first brief arrives through the agreed channel.
If it does not arrive, contact Wideband rather than changing the schedule yourself.

steps.title: Create diagnostics when needed
steps.description: Produce a read-only machine report for troubleshooting. This is a support action, not a completion requirement.
